what: The painted ground (L1 C1): every zone's and arena's ground layers as painted surfaces, ours from nothing (no photo or scan). tools/look/ground_paint.py builds each set's texture arrays (godot/art/ground/, godot/art/arena/<place>/: albedo.png, normal.png, arh.png, seven 1K layers stacked in the order the shaders read them) and checks them (rule 9). A surface is two or three value masses at a large world scale plus big flat shapes (grass clumps, leaves, stones, ruts, chips), each shape one color inside its class's range. Colors are sRGB albedo, set by hand from the boards' and targets' lit and shade colors over the rig's light (the judge's method).
from: (b) the Stage B judge, verdict_sb_r1 'B3's source' and Stage C's order 1 (5 Nov): 'The terrain gets its own painted splat: two or three value masses, big flat clumps, no photo noise'; LOOK_BIBLE rules 1, 4, 5, 8, 9; boards MB4 (wild) and MB3 (town); targets 01, 03, 04, 05, 07, 09, 10, 12. (a) the play camera: 5-8 px per 6-10 cm brush, nothing under about 3 cm.
light_what: the painted-in light's direction in the texture (u = world +x, v = world +z): from the screen's top, a little left (rule 9: the top-lit side, the lit bevel)

mass_sizes.from: rule 10 (shape language: big-medium-small) and the wave-1 judge (04, 05: one size of camo blob); the big masses at 1.6 x a surface's scale_m, islands of the next value at 0.6 x (16% of the tile) and 0.3 x (10%)
